transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30T16:00:00Z
Duration: 49 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Silva (Redwood CSM), Laura Chen (Skybound Head of ML), Marcus O'Hara (Skybound Platform), Priya Raman (Skybound CTO), Evan Li (Skybound Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): kickoff to align POC gates, define success criteria, agree access steps and benchmark schedule.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jared Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jared, AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our SE, and Marco. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Laura Chen: Hi, Laura here.
[00:08] Marcus O'Hara: Marcus.
[00:09] Priya Raman: Priya Raman, CTO.
[00:11] Evan Li: Evan, data science.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Priya D., solutions eng. Great to meet you all.
[00:16] Jared Kim: Great. Goal for today: lock the POC timeline, clarify success criteria and who's owning what for access and benchmarks. We'll keep this tight to leave time for questions.
[00:28] Laura Chen: Sounds good. We're particularly focused on latency and cost — our current in-house cluster hits p50 around 280ms for short summaries, but at scale cost explodes. We want to see if Redwood can match quality while lowering unit cost.
[00:44] Priya Desai: Helpful. When you say "short summaries" — what's your typical sequence length and batch size in production?
[00:51] Evan Li: Mostly 256 tokens input, generation avg 120 tokens. Concurrency spikes to ~50 req/s during business hours, sustained 15-20 off-peak.
[01:03] Priya Desai: Perfect. For benchmarking we'll model 50 req/s sustained with a 95th percentile burst to 120 for a minute to simulate traffic. We'll also run a latency-focused run at 1qps but with low batching to simulate realtime.
[01:20] Marcus O'Hara: On access, our preferred pattern is VPC peering to a dedicated environment, with SSO via Okta and KMS for key management. We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:30] Marco Silva: Noted — we support VPC/Private deployments; we can map the integration checklist. We'll also include a hosted fallback for speed of start if VPC takes extra time.
[01:40] Laura Chen: Timelinewise we want the POC to finish before our November budgeting offsite — so ~8 weeks is the target. Midpoint readout around week 4.
[01:51] Jared Kim: That matches our template. Proposed milestones: Week 0: kickoff+access; Week 1: access verified and sample data ingested; Week 2: initial perf runs; Week 4: midpoint readout (bench results + quality evals); Week 6: regression and tuning; Week 8: exec readout and decision.
[02:10] Priya Raman: Who's doing the quality eval? We'll need to compare against our current model using both ROUGE and a semantic sim score.
[02:17] Priya Desai: SE team will run automated eval harness but we'll need your labeled test set for absolute comparisons. If you can provide 500-1,000 holdout docs that'd be ideal.
[02:28] Evan Li: We can extract a 800-doc slice and share via secure S3 link.
[02:32] Marcus O'Hara: About dataset sharing — can we use presigned URLs? Our compliance team prefers short-lived links and we also need guidance for de-id steps.
[02:40] Priya Desai: Presigned links are fine. We'll provide an ingestion script. For sensitive PII we'll support masked examples, and for the private deployment we can ensure no telemetry leaves the VPC.
[02:50] Laura Chen: Success criteria proposal: 1) Latency p50 < 350ms under 50 req/s with realistic batching; 2) Cost per 1k tokens reduced by at least 20% vs. baseline; 3) Quality delta (semantic sim) within 3% of baseline, or better. If those are met, we'll recommend Redwood for prod.
[03:12] Jared Kim: Those are concrete — we like that. We'll codify: metric definitions, measurement runs, and the scripts used.
[03:20] Marco Silva: Also, we'll run a canary where we route 5% of live traffic through Redwood (if you want) after the midpoint to sanity-check in prod-like conditions. Optional but useful.
[03:31] Priya Raman: We probably can't touch prod yet — but a mirrored pipeline in staging would be ok.
[03:36] Jared Kim: Understood. For the benchmarking plan: Priya (SE) will run two tracks: perf (latency/throughput cost) and quality (eval harness against your holdout). We'll use your 800-doc sample and an augmented synthetic load to hit concurrency patterns.
[03:52] Priya Desai: I'll also test quantized model variants and dedicated vs hosted to show cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll include a spreadsheet with token-level cost breakdowns.
[04:02] Laura Chen: On security: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, SSO SAML flow diagram, KMS key policies, and proof that audit logs can ship to our Splunk instance.
[04:12] Marco Silva: We'll share the security pack tomorrow — SOC2 summary, SAML guide, KMS integration notes, and an audit log forwarder doc.
[04:20] Evan Li: Any limits on token length or streaming? We rely on streaming for UX.
[04:24] Priya Desai: Streaming supported. We'll test chunked responses and KV cache behavior for longer sessions. Note: streaming implementation differs slightly across hosted vs private, so we'll call that out.
[04:37] Speaker 1: (brief crosstalk) can you do the benchmarking in region us-east-1?
[04:40] Jared Kim: Yes, default will be us-east-1. If you need eu or apac we can add later.
[04:45] Laura Chen: Ok. Who signs off on the exec readout? Our execs expect a single slide deck showing perf, cost, and recommended deployment.
[04:53] Jared Kim: We'll produce a 6-slide exec brief: Objectives, Methodology, Perf results, Cost comparison, Risk/Tradeoffs, Recommendation + Ask. Recommended attendees: your CTO and Head of ML.
[05:04] Priya Raman: Good. Can Redwood provide an estimated price band for hosted vs dedicated? Even rough numbers will help our budgeting.
[05:11] Jared Kim: I'll share a pricing matrix that maps throughput to monthly cost; includes reserved capacity options. I'll caveat it as an estimate until we lock the benchmark numbers.
[05:20] Marcus O'Hara: Access checklist — what do you need from us this week to start?
[05:24] Priya Desai: Items: 1) sample dataset S3 link; 2) Okta SSO admin contact and metadata; 3) network owner contact for VPC peering or VPN; 4) list of 3 evaluation metrics and threshold definitions.
[05:36] Marcus O'Hara: I can do the S3 link and network owner by Monday. Okta admin is Priya R.
[05:41] Priya Raman: I'll loop in our security PM to approve the KMS flow.
[05:44] Laura Chen: A question on model selection — do you recommend specific open models or Redwood-provided variants?
[05:50] Priya Desai: We'll recommend 2-3 variants optimized for your latency/quality target: a quantized medium-size variant for cost-efficiency and a full fp16 for headroom. We'll include recommended kernel/runtime settings.
[06:02] Evan Li: For eval — can you surface per-doc examples where quality regresses? That helps our product team triage.
[06:07] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll include a per-example diff report tied to the holdout IDs.
[06:12] Jared Kim: Ok let's talk gating: what kills the POC early? e.g., if we can't get access in week 1 or if quality delta is >10% after week 4? Thoughts?
[06:23] Laura Chen: Access delays are our biggest fear. If network/SSO/KMS isn't in place by week 2 we might pause.
[06:29] Priya Desai: We'll bring a hosted fallback so tests can start while private setup continues. The hosted runs will have masked telemetry and no persistent storage to meet compliance while you get VPC review done.
[06:41] Speaker 2: (mumble) also to note, we want to test KV cache effectiveness for repeated queries.
[06:45] Priya Desai: Yes we'll include cache hit-rate experiments and estimate per-token savings.
[06:51] Marco Silva: For midpoint review we'll present: current perf, quality diffs, cost per 1k tokens, and risks & blocker list.
[06:59] Marcus O'Hara: For scheduling the midpoint can we aim for week-of-Nov-9? That gives buffer for access.
[07:04] Jared Kim: Noted — we'll propose concrete dates by Friday.
[07:08] Priya Desai: Quick logistics: I'll need API keys scoped to benchmarking only; if using VPC we'll provide a containerized harness.
[07:16] Evan Li: About telemetry — does Redwood collect model inputs by default? Our policy is to not retain PII.
[07:21] Marco Silva: Default telemetry is minimal; for private deployments telemetry can be disabled. We'll document retention windows.
[07:27] Laura Chen: Any legal / contract items to surface early? Data processing addendum?
[07:31] Jared Kim: We'll attach a DPS/DPA template and a short SOW for the POC with cancellation terms.
[07:36] Priya Raman: Sounds good. One more question: do you support custom kernels or extensions for our in-house models?
[07:43] Priya Desai: We can evaluate model bring-your-own options for private deployments; for hosted we support curated open models and Redwood-verified variants.
[07:51] Jared Kim: Alright let's recap: action items and owners. Priya D runs benchmark harness and shares by 2026-10-07; Jared sends pricing and security pack by 2026-10-04; Marcus provides S3 sample and network contact by 2026-10-03. Midpoint review week of 2026-11-09; exec readout target week of 2026-11-30.
[08:15] Laura Chen: That timeline aligns with our budget cycle. Thanks.
[08:18] Jared Kim: Thanks all — we'll follow up with meeting notes and the security pack tomorrow.
[08:22] (meeting ends, some cross chatter)
